'''Isabel Alicia Hubard Escalera '''is a Mexican mathematician in the Institute of Mathematics of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM).

== Early life and education ==
As a child, Isabel Alicia Hubard wanted to be a bullfighter. She has said of her family, "My mother is an engineer and my father an accountant. My brother is a mathematician and my sister a physicist. I never thought that I would like math. I simply found it easy and fun, but nothing more. However, my mathematics teacher in junior high and high school, Óscar Chávez, inspired me."<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=http://www.ancefn.org.ar/biblioteca/docs/YOUNG%2013DIC15.pdf|title=Young Women Scientists: A bright future for the Americas|last=Zubieta García|first=Judith|date=November 2015|publisher=Inter-American Network of Academies of Sciences|isbn=978-607-8379-24-8|access-date=2017-01-24|archive-date=2018-05-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180508144037/http://www.ancefn.org.ar/biblioteca/docs/YOUNG%2013DIC15.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hubard Escalera began her studies in the Faculty of Sciences of the UNAM, where in 2001, she graduated in [[Mathematics]] with a baccalaureate thesis titled ''Polyhedra colored with cyclic orders''.<ref name="vuelven">{{Cite web|url=http://www.comunicacion.amc.edu.mx/comunicados/vuelven-los-poliedros-a-ser-retomados-por-los-matematicos/|title=Coordinación de Comunicación y Divulgación, AMC - Vuelven los Poliedros a Ser Retomados por los Matemáticos|last=Zúñiga Murrieta|first=Nancy|date=2013-04-05|website=www.comunicacion.amc.edu.mx|publisher=Academia Mexicana de Ciencias|language=es-MX|access-date=2017-01-24}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://132.248.9.195/pd2001/299035/Index.html|title=Tesis que para Obtener el Titulo de Matematica, Presenta: Isabel Alicia Hubard Escalera|last=|first=|date=|website=132.248.9.195|publisher=|access-date=2017-01-24}}</ref> It was written in the Institute of Mathematics of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico|UNAM]], where she carried out investigations related to the combinatorial properties of [[Discrete geometry|discrete geometrical]] objects.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.matem.unam.mx/fsd/hubard|title=Isabel Hubard — Instituto de Matemáticas {{!}} UNAM|website=www.matem.unam.mx|language=es|access-date=2017-01-24}}</ref><ref name="loreal">{{Cite web|url=http://www.dgcs.unam.mx/boletin/bdboletin/2013_280.html|title=Isabel Hubard Escalera, primera matemática en obtener la beca L'Oréal-UNESCO-AMC|date=2013-05-05|website=www.dgcs.unam.mx|publisher=Boletín UNAM-DGCS-280 Ciudad Universitaria.|access-date=2017-01-24}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.jornada.unam.mx/2015/06/26/ciencias/a02n1cie|title=La Jornada: Combatir los mitos que rodean a las matemáticas, el gran reto|last=Mateos-Vega|first=Mónica|date=2015-06-26|website=La Jornada|access-date=2017-01-24}}</ref> Her undergraduate advisor was Javier Bracho Carpizo.<ref name=":0" />

In 2007, she earned a Ph.D. from [[York University]] in [[Canada]], with a dissertation titled ''From geometry to groups and back: the study of highly symmetric polytopes''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://convocation.students.yorku.ca/sites/convocation/files/pdf/february2008.pdf|title=Convocation|date=February 2008|website=York University|page=13|access-date=2017-01-24}}</ref><ref name="Hubard2007">{{cite book|author=Isabel A. Hubard|title=From Geometry to Groups and Back: The Study of Highly Symmetric Polytopes|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2rzJhDD3eycC|year=2007|publisher=York University (Canada)|isbn=978-0-494-45997-3}}</ref>

== Career ==
Hubard Escalera investigates the study of symmetries of combinatorial objects.<ref name="vuelven" />

She has been the organiser of the [[Mexico City]] Mathematics Olympiad in Mexico City since 2013, an organization that played a prominent role in recent national competitions, achieving the first place of the 2017, 2018 and 2019 Olimpiadas Mexicanas de Matematicas (OMM), and won the basic education national competitions (OMMEB) the same years.<ref name=":2" /> She is the delegate for Mexico City in the Mexican Mathematics Olympiad of the Mexican Mathematics Society.<ref name=":1" /> She has also been the leader of the Mexican team at EGMO since 2014, competition in which Mexico has won two gold medals, with Isabel mentoring the girls.

==Recognition==

She was awarded the Kovalevskaia Fund Prize in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kovfund.org/winners.pdf|title=Winners of the Kovalevskaia Fund Prizes and Scholarships since 2005|last=|first=|year=2015|publisher=The Kovalevskaia Fund|access-date=2017-01-17}}</ref>

In 2012 she was the first Mexican mathematician to receive the L´Oréal-UNESCO-AMC Fellowship in the area of Exact Sciences for her work, titled ''Algebra, combinatorics and geometry of abstract two-orbit polytopes''.<ref name="vuelven"/><ref name="loreal"/> The Fellowship is awarded to "promote the participation of women in science for advanced scientific studies in universities or other recognized Mexican institutions in the areas of exact sciences, natural sciences and engineering and technology."

She was elected to the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amc.mx/amc/membresia/MATEMATICAS2022.pdf|title=Mathematics section members|publisher=Mexican Academy of Sciences|year=2022|access-date=2022-12-05}}</ref>
